item.text: {"question_id":"5B.2","answer":"The supplied record does not establish that Sisi appointed qualified economic professionals through credible processes or retained/replaced them based on performance. It does show Sisi chaired the Supreme Council for Investment, issued implementation directions, and sponsored proposed mechanisms involving regulator independence, state-company restructuring, binding decisions, and periodic reporting; these indicate active coordination and some intended delegation, but several measures remained proposals or assignments, with no appointment criteria, qualifications, dismissal reasons, or performance-based retention evidence (BATCH-0006-E020; BATCH-0006-E021). The broader institutional context is adverse to demonstrating independent professional bodies: policymaking was dominated by the presidency, military, and intelligence agencies, while military-managed civilian activities had substantial autonomy in project and partner selection (BATCH-0008-E001; BATCH-0009-R10-E001; BATCH-0009-R10-E002). The Carnegie evidence reports that Sisi viewed the military as competent and loyal, but this does not prove a performance-based personnel system. Training evidence concerns anti-trafficking specialists rather than economic appointments and is not probative of this question (BATCH-0008-E007; BATCH-0023-E015). Overall, the answer remains indeterminate, with evidence of presidentially directed economic administration and proposed institutional delegation, but no demonstrated meritocratic selection, operational independence of economic professionals, or performance-based personnel decisions.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E020","BATCH-0006-E021"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E001","BATCH-0009-R10-E001","BATCH-0009-R10-E002","BATCH-0008-E007","BATCH-0023-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence identifies economic ministers or other economic professionals, their qualifications, appointment procedures, delegated authority, dismissal reasons, or performance-based retention.","The investment-council measures include proposals, studies, assignments, and intended reporting mechanisms; the record does not establish completed implementation or actual operational independence.","The military evidence concerns institutional dominance, delegation, autonomy, and stated perceptions of competence and loyalty, not a complete economic-personnel record.","Anti-trafficking training records document specialist capacity-building outside economic administration and cannot substantiate qualified economic appointments or performance-based personnel management.","The conclusion is limited to the supplied evidence and the 2023 period, with relevant institutional context extending from earlier years."],"corrections_made":["Removed anti-trafficking training and prosecution-training evidence as direct support for qualified economic leadership; retained it only as non-probative qualifying context.","Added BATCH-0006-E020 and BATCH-0006-E021 as the strongest contrary or qualifying evidence of presidentially directed economic administration and proposed delegation mechanisms.","Recast the military evidence to avoid claiming a demonstrated loyalist or competent personnel system; it supports stated rationale, institutional dominance, and autonomy only.","Preserved the distinction between proposals and implementation, and between administrative activity and proof of meritocratic selection, independence, or performance-based retention."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if appointment records, ministerial biographies, cabinet turnover explanations, civil-service procedures, central-bank governance records, or evidence of actual implementation of the proposed independence and reporting mechanisms become available.","Reopen if evidence links economic officials' retention or replacement to measurable performance rather than presidential confidence, loyalty, or institutional affiliation."]}
